payload.rationale: Gasoline prices have risen significantly in the first half of September 2026, which will likely add upward pressure to the headline CPI. With core inflation recently running around 0.3%, the combination of positive energy contributions and sticky core inflation makes a print of 0.3% or higher very likely.
limitations: Only first half of September gasoline data is available; late-month price movements are unknown.
Core CPI components, particularly shelter and services, can be volatile and are not directly observable in high-frequency data.
Seasonal adjustment factors can unpredictably alter the final published month-over-month changes.
payload.partition_justification: The scenarios are partitioned based on the two main drivers of headline CPI uncertainty for the remainder of the month: the trajectory of energy prices (specifically gasoline) and the underlying core inflation rate.

scenarios.description: Gasoline prices remain at their mid-September highs or increase further, while core inflation remains stable around 0.2% to 0.3%.
scenarios.rationale: With gasoline prices up significantly in early September, a sustained high level will add roughly 0.15% to 0.20% to headline CPI. Combined with a 0.2%+ core, headline CPI will easily exceed 0.25%, rounding to 0.3% or higher.

scenarios.description: Gasoline prices retrace significantly in the second half of September, neutralizing the early-month gains, but core inflation remains firm at 0.2% to 0.3%.
scenarios.rationale: If energy's contribution drops to near zero, headline CPI will closely track core CPI. A core print of 0.2% to 0.3% leaves the headline print hovering around the 0.25% rounding threshold, making it a coin toss or slightly favored to hit 0.3%.
unknowns: Magnitude of potential gasoline price retracement
Rounding effects on the final index

scenarios.description: Energy prices drop in late September and core inflation surprises to the downside (0.1% or lower).
scenarios.rationale: A combination of falling energy prices and cooling core inflation (e.g., a drop in shelter costs) would pull headline CPI down to 0.1% or 0.2%, failing to exceed the >0.2% threshold.
unknowns: Potential downside surprises in shelter or used car prices
